summary: El Salvador’s pledge is to restore or rehabilitate 1,000,000 ha of degraded agricultural and ecosystem landscapes in 2035–2040. AFOLU transition measures cover 818,421 ha and are linked to a cumulative 50,857.5 Kton CO 2 Eq reduction for 2035–2040, counted from 2015. The headline area equals 49.1% of land—66.2% of mapped forest in area terms—and includes agricultural land. Restoration covers 18,930 ha of riparian forest and a 30% forest-cover increase in hydroelectric sub-basins. Conservation references 207,387 ha of Ramsar sites and a 606,541.78-ha forest inventory. Agriculture includes 27,600 ha of green sugarcane harvest—6.3% of mapped agriculture and 35% of sugarcane area—3% annual expansion, 50,000 ha of training and 10,000 ha under good practices, 500 producers, 2,600 and 400 manzanas of soil recovery, and 626 kt CO₂eq of livestock-emission reductions by 2035. LULUCF scenarios report 144,000 and 144,290 ha by 2035 and 275,000 ha by 2040.
